evidence.summary: register() lowercases the email, draws a 16-byte random salt, stores a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash (100,000 iterations), role 'user' and id len(USERS)+1.
register() assigns USERS[email] without checking whether the email exists, so registering an existing email replaces that account and its password.

login() recomputes the hash and compares with '!=' (not constant time); unknown email and wrong password both raise ValueError('bad credentials'); success stores a token_urlsafe(24) in SESSIONS mapped to the user id.
USERS (email -> record) and SESSIONS (token -> user id) are module-level in-memory dicts; there is no logout, no session lookup and no expiry in the file.

architecture.backend: single Python module with module-level state

features.name: Email and password registration
features.description: Create an account from an email address and a password.
features.observed_behaviour: Email is lowercased; a salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash is stored with role 'user' and a sequential integer id. Nothing is returned.
features.business_logic: Email is case-insensitive. No password rules. No duplicate check: an existing email is silently overwritten (A-E02).
features.integration: Needs the unified user store and the unified role set (role 'user').

features.name: Password login with session token
features.description: Sign in with email and password and receive a session token.
features.observed_behaviour: Looks up the lowercased email, recomputes the hash, raises ValueError('bad credentials') on any failure, otherwise returns a random token stored in SESSIONS.
features.business_logic: Same error for unknown email and wrong password. Non-constant-time comparison. Tokens never expire and cannot be revoked (no logout).
features.integration: Needs the unified session mechanism, whoami and logout.

auth.session: opaque random token in a server-side in-memory map, no expiry
auth.model: one role string per user, no permission checks in this app

error_handling.behaviour: no error; the account is replaced

unknowns: Only accounts.py was provided; whether Passbook has password reset, email verification or logout elsewhere is unknown (the user could share the rest of the app).
